title: printf and format: strict, raise on a format that does not fit
verdict: recorded: printf and format are black boxes that may raise
description: `printf(fmt, …)` (C's format strings) and `format(fmt, …)` (`{}` fields) are NULL when any argument is NULL, the format included.

Both raise an Invalid Input Error when a field does not fit its value (`printf('%d', 'x')`, `format('{:d}', 'x')`) or has no value (`printf('%d')`, `format('{} {}', 1)`). A format without fields ignores its values: `printf('abc', 1)` is `abc`.

`printf` formats a signed integer as a BIGINT whatever its width: `printf('%x', -1::TINYINT)` is `ffffffffffffffff`, while `format('{:x}', -1)` is `-1`. A boolean is `true`/`false` under `%s` and `1` under `%d`.
reference: `printf` and `format` of a format and one value are black boxes (#328): strict, may raise (a domain error in `verify`), and a string where they do not. The value is an integer, string or boolean (`BlackBox.Ty.atom`): a double's code and a date are integers in the model, which the function could not tell apart. More values are refused.

evidence.sql: SELECT printf('%d', NULL), printf(NULL, 1), printf('%s', NULL), format('{}-{}', 1, NULL), format(NULL, 1)

evidence.observed: Invalid Input Error: Invalid type specifier "d" for formatting a value of type string
Invalid Input Error: Argument index "1" out of range

evidence.sql: SELECT printf('%s', true), printf('%d', true), format('{}', true)
